"""Checking a server launched as a subprocess over stdio."""

from __future__ import annotations

from mcp import ClientSession, StdioServerParameters
from mcp.client.stdio import stdio_client

from mcpcheck.cases import Case, Mismatch, compare


async def check_command(command: list[str], cases: list[Case]) -> list[Mismatch]:
    """Launch `command`, call every case's tool in order and return the mismatches."""
    program, *args = command
    mismatches: list[Mismatch] = []
    async with stdio_client(StdioServerParameters(command=program, args=args)) as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            for case in cases:
                result = await session.call_tool(case.tool, case.arguments)
                mismatch = compare(case, result)
                if mismatch is not None:
                    mismatches.append(mismatch)
    return mismatches

### Test MCP Server with In-Memory Client

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/get-started

This Python code demonstrates how to test your MCP server using an in-memory client. It connects directly to the server object without needing a subprocess or network transport.

```python
import pytest
from mcp import Client

from server import mcp


@pytest.mark.anyio
async def test_add() -> None:
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        result = await client.call_tool("add", {"a": 1, "b": 2})
        assert result.structured_content == {"result": 3}

```

```python
        async with ClientSession(*client_streams) as session:
```

### Testing utilities > create_connected_server_and_client_session removed

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/migration

The create_connected_server_and_client_session helper has been removed in favor of using mcp.client.Client directly. The Client class accepts a Server or MCPServer instance, handles in-memory transport, and supports configuration parameters such as callbacks, timeouts, and version negotiation modes. Note that Client defaults to a modern negotiation mode that may trigger NoBackChannelError for tests relying on server-initiated requests; use mode='legacy' to maintain v1 behavior.

    """Connector for the stream-backed paths (URL, user-supplied ``Transport``)."""

    async def connect(exit_stack: AsyncExitStack, _mode: ConnectMode, _raise_exceptions: bool) -> Dispatcher[Any]:

def _connect_inproc(server: Server[Any]) -> _Connector:
    """Connector for an in-process ``Server``: legacy mode drives the stream loop via
    ``InMemoryTransport``; any other mode drives the modern per-request path through a
    ``DirectDispatcher`` peer pair (no streams, no JSON-RPC framing, no initialize handshake)."""

    async def connect(exit_stack: AsyncExitStack, mode: ConnectMode, raise_exceptions: bool) -> Dispatcher[Any]:
        if mode == "legacy":
            transport = InMemoryTransport(server, raise_exceptions=raise_exceptions)
            read_stream, write_stream = await exit_stack.enter_async_context(transport)
            return JSONRPCDispatcher(read_stream, write_stream)
        lifespan_state = await exit_stack.enter_async_context(server.lifespan(server))
        client_disp, server_disp = create_direct_dispatcher_pair(raise_handler_exceptions=raise_exceptions)
        tg = await exit_stack.enter_async_context(anyio.create_task_group())
        exit_stack.callback(server_disp.close)
        on_request = modern_on_request(server, lifespan_state)
        await tg.start(server_disp.run, on_request, _no_inbound_client_notifications)
        return client_disp

### Define MCP Server with Tool and Resource

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/troubleshooting

Setup for an MCP server with a tool and a resource that raise custom exceptions when inputs are invalid.

```python
from mcp.server import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ResourceNotFoundError, ToolError

mcp = MCPServer("Weather")

FORECASTS = {"London": "Rain.", "Cairo": "Sun."}


@mcp.tool()
def forecast(city: str) -> str:
    """Today's forecast for one city."""
    if city not in FORECASTS:
        raise ToolError(f"No forecast for {city!r}.")
    return FORECASTS[city]


@mcp.resource("weather://{city}")
def report(city: str) -> str:
    """The full report for one city."""
    if city not in FORECASTS:
        raise ResourceNotFoundError(f"No forecast for {city!r}.")
    return f"{city}: {FORECASTS[city]}"
```

--------------------------------

### Importing MCP Error Classes

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/servers/handling-errors

Required imports for handling and raising specific MCP-related exceptions.

```python
from mcp import MCPError
from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ToolError, ResourceError, ResourceNotFoundError
```

--------------------------------

### Call a tool with the MCP client

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/client

Demonstrates defining a tool on an MCPServer and invoking it from an MCP Client, including processing the returned content and structured data.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

from mcp import Client
from mcp.server import MCPServer
from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ToolError
from mcp.types import TextContent

mcp = MCPServer("Bookshop")


class Book(BaseModel):
    title: str
    author: str
    year: int


@mcp.tool()
def lookup_book(title: str) -> Book:
    """Look up a book by its exact title."""
    if title != "Dune":
        raise ToolError(f"No book titled {title!r} in the catalog.")
    return Book(title="Dune", author="Frank Herbert", year=1965)


async def main() -> None:
    async with Client(mcp) as client:
        result = await client.call_tool("lookup_book", {"title": "Dune"})

        for block in result.content:
            if isinstance(block, TextContent):
                print(block.text)

        print(result.structured_content)
        print(result.is_error)
```

--------------------------------

### Inspect Tool Execution Results

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/troubleshooting

Illustrates how tool errors are returned as result objects rather than raised exceptions.

```python
result.is_error  # True
result.content   # [TextContent(text="Error executing tool forecast: No forecast for 'Atlantis'.")]
result.structured_content  # None
```

### Migration > MCPError handling

Source: https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/migration

Raising an MCPError within an @mcp.tool() handler now surfaces as a top-level JSON-RPC error, preserving the original error code, message, and data. This replaces the previous behavior where such errors were caught and returned as a standard tool result. For general tool execution failures, developers should continue to use ToolError or return a CallToolResult with is_error set to true.
